summary: Chūta Itō (1867–1954) was a history and archaeology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1889–1892), First Higher School, Tokyo School of Foreign Languages, and Sakura High School, later holding posts at the University of Tokyo (~1905–1928) and Waseda University.

Clara Sue Kidwell (1941–2025) studied at the University of Oklahoma (master's ~1963–1966, Ph.D. ~1966–1970). Her career included posts at UC Berkeley (~1974–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian (~1993–1995), the University of Oklahoma, and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

Clare Carlisle (born 1977) works in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002), and has held posts as Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and professor at King's College London (~2011).

Linguist Claude Hagège (born 1936) studied at ENS, Collège Louis-le-Grand, École des Langues Orientales, Paris Descartes, and under André Martinet. His posts included CNRS (~1965–1970), the University of Poitiers (1970–1987), Collège de France (1988–2006), and EPHE (~1982–2006).

Claude Jacques (1929–2018) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying under George Cœdès (~1956–1969). He served as director at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (~1970–1973) and taught epigraphy and history at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1973–1998).

Claude Lévi-Strauss (1908–2009) studied at Paris Law Faculty and under Marcel Mauss. His career included posts at the University of São Paulo (~1935–1939), EPHE (~1948–1974), EHESS (~1948–1982), and the Collège de France chair of Anthropologie sociale (1959–1982).

Claude-Auguste Court (1793–1880) was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1812–1813) and the École polytechnique, later serving as an Engineer Officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army (~1827–1843).
Claudia Benthien (born 1965) is a linguistics scholar. She studied at Washington University in St. Louis (1993–1994) and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~2005).
Claudia Weber is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under teacher Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

Claudius Buchanan (1766–1815) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow (1782), the University of Cambridge (1791), and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1791–1795), later serving as Vice-Provost at Fort William College (1801).

Claus Oetke (1947–2019) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his PhD (~1968–1973) and Habilitation (~1974–1983) at the University of Hamburg, and served as head of Indology at the University of Stockholm (1993–2014).

Claus Vogel (1933–2012) studied Indology and Tibetology at Marburg (PhD ~1952–1956; Habilitation ~1961–1964) and Deccan College. He held posts at the University of Marburg, the University of Göttingen, and served as Ordinarius at the University of Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle (born 1977) works in Indology and history and archaeology. She held academic posts at the University of Canterbury in 2007 and from 2020 to 2025.

Clyde Kluckhohn (1905–1960) studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Oxford, Vienna, and Harvard. He held academic posts at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Colette Caillat (1921–2007) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Louis Renou, Jules Bloch, and Walther Schubring. She held posts at CNRS (~1951–1965), University of Lyon (1960–1966), and the Sorbonne (1967–1988).

Colette Sciberras works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and also studied under traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is an Indology and philosophy researcher who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria (both attested 2002).
Colin Mackenzie (1754–1821) studied at Dollar Academy and served as Surveyor-General at the Survey of India from approximately 1815 to 1821.
Colin Turnbull (1924–1994) was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at Westminster School (~1936–1942), Magdalen College (~1942–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951).

Collett Cox is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Tokyo, Ryukoku, and Columbia (PhD) under Alex Wayman and Yoshito S. Hakeda. She held a professorship at the University of Washington (attested 1999, 2017).
